formulas.title: Wigner 6j Symbol Three-Angular-Momentum Recoupling Transformation
formulas.description: Relates the two distinct associative coupling schemes for three quantum angular momenta $(j_1, j_2, j_3)$ summing to total angular momentum $J$ via the rotationally invariant Wigner $6j$ recoupling symbol.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Provides the $M$-independent orthogonal transformation connecting intermediate-coupling bases in three-body and many-body quantum systems.
formulas.intuitive_summary: When adding three quantum spins, grouping the first two versus the last two gives different intermediate labels; the Wigner 6j symbol translates exactly between those two perspectives.
formulas.interpretation: Invariant under any permutation of columns and under exchanging upper and lower entries in any two columns (24 tetrahedral symmetries), the $6j$ symbol vanishes unless all four triads $(j_1, j_2, J_{12})$, $(j_1, J, J_{23})$, $(j_3, j_2, J_{23})$, and $(j_3, J, J_{12})$ satisfy the triangle inequality.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from contracting four Clebsch-Gordan coefficients (or Wigner $3j$ symbols) over all magnetic projections, eliminating orientation dependence by $SU(2)$ invariance.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Equivalently written in terms of the Racah $W$-coefficient via $\begin{Bmatrix} j_1 & j_2 & J_{12} \\ j_3 & J & J_{23} \end{Bmatrix} = (-1)^{j_1+j_2+j_3+J} W(j_1 j_2 J j_3; J_{12} J_{23})$. In the semiclassical large-$j$ limit (Ponzano-Regge formula), oscillates with the cosine of the Regge action of a Euclidean tetrahedron.

J_{12}.name: First-Pair Intermediate Angular Momentum
J_{12}.description: Coupled angular momentum quantum number formed by combining $j_1$ and $j_2$ first.

J_{23}.name: Second-Pair Intermediate Angular Momentum
J_{23}.description: Coupled angular momentum quantum number formed by combining $j_2$ and $j_3$ first.

J.name: Total Three-Body Angular Momentum
J.description: Conserved total angular momentum quantum number of the three-subsystem state.

\\begin{Bmatrix} j_1 & j_2 & J_{12} \\\\.name: Wigner 6j Symbol
\\begin{Bmatrix} j_1 & j_2 & J_{12} \\\\.description: Real, $M$-independent recoupling invariant exhibiting 24 tetrahedral symmetries.

formulas.title: Slater Determinant Many-Electron Wavefunction
formulas.description: Constructs an antisymmetrized $N$-electron trial wavefunction $\Psi_{\mathrm{SD}}$ as the normalized determinant of $N$ orthonormal single-particle spin-orbitals $\phi_i(\mathbf{x}_j)$ evaluated at electron space-spin coordinates $\mathbf{x}_j = (\mathbf{r}_j, \sigma_j)$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: A Slater determinant is the simplest many-fermion wavefunction built from single-particle orbitals that automatically changes sign under the exchange of any two electrons.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Arranging one-electron orbitals into a matrix determinant guarantees that swapping any two electrons flips the wavefunction's sign and forbids two electrons from occupying the same quantum state.
formulas.interpretation: Exchanging coordinates $\mathbf{x}_j \leftrightarrow \mathbf{x}_k$ swaps two columns of the matrix $[\phi_i(\mathbf{x}_j)]$, multiplying $\Psi_{\mathrm{SD}}$ by $-1$ and forcing the amplitude to vanish identically whenever two electrons share identical spin-orbitals or coincide at the same point with parallel spin (creating the Fermi exchange hole).
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from the fermionic antisymmetry postulate under the symmetric permutation group $S_N$ for indistinguishable spin-1/2 particles.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Exact for strictly non-interacting fermions in an external potential. For interacting electrons, a single Slater determinant captures exact exchange but neglects dynamical Coulomb correlation, requiring multi-determinant configuration interaction expansions to reach the exact eigenstate.

\\Psi_{\\mathrm{SD}}(\\mathbf{x}_1, \\do.name: Slater Determinant Wavefunction
\\Psi_{\\mathrm{SD}}(\\mathbf{x}_1, \\do.description: Normalized antisymmetric $N$-electron wavefunction over combined space-spin coordinates.

N.name: Number of Electrons
N.description: Total number of interacting fermions in the atom, molecule, or unit cell.

\\phi_i(\\mathbf{x}_j).name: Single-Electron Spin-Orbital
\\phi_i(\\mathbf{x}_j).description: Orthonormal $i$-th single-particle spin-orbital evaluated at the space-spin coordinate $\mathbf{x}_j$ of the $j$-th electron.

\\mathbf{x}_j.name: Electron Space-Spin Coordinate
\\mathbf{x}_j.description: Composite coordinate $(\mathbf{r}_j, \sigma_j)$ combining spatial position and spin projection for electron $j$.

formulas.title: Canonical Hartree-Fock Integro-Differential Equation
formulas.description: Governs the variationally optimal canonical spin-orbitals $\phi_i(\mathbf{x})$ and orbital energies $\varepsilon_i$ of a single Slater determinant via the self-consistent Fock operator $\hat{F} = \hat{h} + \hat{J} - \hat{K}$ combining one-electron core, direct Hartree Coulomb, and nonlocal Fock exchange operators.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Each electron moves in the static nuclear field plus the averaged electrostatic repulsion of all electrons, corrected by a purely quantum nonlocal exchange interaction that keeps like-spin electrons apart.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Hartree-Fock reduces a tangled many-electron problem into one-electron equations where every electron feels the average charge of the others minus a quantum Pauli-exclusion discount.
formulas.interpretation: Because both $\hat{J}$ and $\hat{K}$ depend on the occupied orbitals $\{\phi_j\}$, the equation is nonlinear and must be iterated to self-consistency; the $i=j$ self-interaction terms in $\hat{J}$ and $\hat{K}$ cancel identically, and the diagonal Lagrange multipliers $\varepsilon_i$ approximate negative vertical ionization potentials via Koopmans' theorem.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived by stationary Rayleigh-Ritz functional variation of $\langle \Psi_{\mathrm{SD}} | \hat{H}_e | \Psi_{\mathrm{SD}} \rangle$ with respect to $\phi_i^*(\mathbf{x})$ under orthonormality constraints, followed by a unitary rotation among occupied orbitals that diagonalizes the Lagrange multiplier matrix.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Becomes exact for one-electron systems (where $\hat{J} - \hat{K} = 0$) and in the high-density weak-coupling limit of the homogeneous electron gas, but fails during homolytic covalent bond dissociation where restricted single-determinant states mix ionic and covalent character.

\\hat{F}.name: Fock Operator
\\hat{F}.description: Effective one-electron self-consistent mean-field Hamiltonian operator $\hat{h} + \hat{J} - \hat{K}$.

\\phi_i(\\mathbf{x}).name: Canonical Hartree-Fock Spin-Orbital
\\phi_i(\\mathbf{x}).description: Eigenfunction of the Fock operator representing the $i$-th occupied or virtual single-electron state.

\\varepsilon_i.name: Canonical Orbital Energy
\\varepsilon_i.description: Eigenvalue of the Fock operator approximating minus the vertical ionization energy for occupied states under Koopmans' theorem.

\\hat{h}.name: Core One-Electron Hamiltonian
\\hat{h}.description: Sum of single-electron kinetic energy $-(\hbar^2/2m)\nabla^2$ and external nuclear Coulomb attraction.

\\hat{J}.name: Direct Coulomb (Hartree) Operator
\\hat{J}.description: Local electrostatic repulsion operator generated by the total electron charge density of all occupied orbitals.

\\hat{K}.name: Nonlocal Fock Exchange Operator
\\hat{K}.description: Integral exchange operator arising from Slater-determinant antisymmetry that couples like-spin orbitals and cancels self-interaction.

formulas.title: Löwdin Electron Correlation Energy
formulas.description: Defines the nonrelativistic electron correlation energy $E_{\mathrm{corr}}$ as the difference between the exact ground-state eigenvalue $E_{\mathrm{exact}}$ of the clamped-nuclei electronic Hamiltonian and the complete-basis Hartree-Fock variational energy $E_{\mathrm{HF}}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Correlation energy quantifies the energy lowering achieved when electrons dynamically avoid one another beyond the mean-field and Pauli-exchange description of a single Slater determinant.
formulas.intuitive_summary: It is the exact energy discount that real electrons gain by dodging each other's instantaneous electric repulsion instead of seeing only a smeared-out average cloud.
formulas.interpretation: By the Rayleigh-Ritz variational theorem, $E_{\mathrm{HF}} \ge E_{\mathrm{exact}}$ strictly, so $E_{\mathrm{corr}} \le 0$ for every bound many-electron ground state; although $E_{\mathrm{corr}}$ is typically less than 1% of the total atomic energy, it is comparable to chemical bond dissociation energies and dispersion interactions.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Defined by Per-Olov Löwdin as the exact energetic benchmark separating mean-field single-determinant theory from full many-body quantum mechanics.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Vanishes identically ($E_{\mathrm{corr}} = 0$) for any one-electron system. Diverges in relative importance in strongly correlated Mott insulators, stretched covalent bonds, and van der Waals complexes where dynamical or static correlation dominates.

E_{\\mathrm{corr}}.name: Electron Correlation Energy
E_{\\mathrm{corr}}.description: Non-positive energy difference capturing all instantaneous dynamical and multi-reference static electron correlation.

E_{\\mathrm{exact}}.name: Exact Nonrelativistic Ground-State Energy
E_{\\mathrm{exact}}.description: Lowest eigenvalue of the exact clamped-nuclei electronic Schrödinger equation.

E_{\\mathrm{HF}}.name: Complete-Basis Hartree-Fock Energy
E_{\\mathrm{HF}}.description: Variational minimum energy attainable by any single Slater determinant in the complete basis-set limit.

formulas.title: Hohenberg-Kohn Variational Energy Functional
formulas.description: Expresses the ground-state total energy $E[n]$ of an interacting electronic system in an external potential $V_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathbf{r})$ as a variational functional of the three-dimensional electron density $n(\mathbf{r})$ using the universal Hohenberg-Kohn functional $F_{\mathrm{HK}}[n]$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The exact ground-state energy of any interacting electron system can be found by minimizing a universal density functional plus the classical coupling of the density to the external potential.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Instead of tracking a impossibly complex 3N-dimensional wavefunction, nature's ground-state energy is completely fixed by a simple three-dimensional map of where the electrons are concentrated.
formulas.interpretation: In Levy-Lieb constrained-search form, $F_{\mathrm{HK}}[n] = \min_{\Psi \to n} \langle \Psi | \hat{T} + \hat{V}_{ee} | \Psi \rangle$ is universal—identical for atoms, proteins, and crystals—while system-specific geometry enters solely through $\int V_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathbf{r}) n(\mathbf{r}) d^3r$; any trial density $n(\mathbf{r}) \ge 0$ with $\int n(\mathbf{r}) d^3r = N$ satisfies $E[n] \ge E_0$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Established by the 1964 Hohenberg-Kohn reductio ad absurdum uniqueness proof and the quantum Rayleigh-Ritz variational principle over $N$-representable densities.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Strictly exact for nondegenerate time-independent ground states in local scalar external potentials; generalized to degenerate ground states via Levy-Lieb search, to spin-polarized systems via spin densities $(n_\uparrow, n_\downarrow)$, and to finite temperatures via Mermin's free-energy functional.

E[n].name: Total Energy Density Functional
E[n].description: Total electronic ground-state energy evaluated as a functional of the trial three-dimensional electron density $n(\mathbf{r})$.

F_{\\mathrm{HK}}[n].name: Universal Hohenberg-Kohn Functional
F_{\\mathrm{HK}}[n].description: System-independent functional encompassing interacting kinetic energy and electron-electron Coulomb repulsion.

V_{\\mathrm{ext}}(\\mathbf{r}).name: External Scalar Potential
V_{\\mathrm{ext}}(\\mathbf{r}).description: External potential energy acting on an electron at position $\mathbf{r}$, typically from atomic nuclei and applied electric fields.

n(\\mathbf{r}).name: Three-Dimensional Electron Number Density
n(\\mathbf{r}).description: Probability density of finding an electron per unit volume at spatial coordinate $\mathbf{r}$, normalized to $\int n(\mathbf{r}) d^3r = N$.

formulas.title: Kohn-Sham Auxiliary Single-Particle Equation
formulas.description: Defines the self-consistent single-particle Schrödinger equation for auxiliary non-interacting Kohn-Sham orbitals $\psi_i(\mathbf{r})$ moving in a local effective potential $V_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{r})$ that reproduces the exact ground-state electron density $n(\mathbf{r}) = \sum_{i=1}^N |\psi_i(\mathbf{r})|^2$ of the interacting system.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Kohn-Sham theory maps the intractable interacting many-electron problem onto an auxiliary gas of non-interacting electrons in a local effective potential whose orbitals recover the exact density and kinetic shell structure.
formulas.intuitive_summary: By inventing fictitious non-interacting electrons moving through a carefully tuned local potential, Kohn and Sham made exact density functional theory computationally solvable at cubic cost.
formulas.interpretation: Unlike Hartree-Fock, $V_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{r})$ is a purely local multiplicative potential; the occupied Kohn-Sham orbitals determine the exact density $n(\mathbf{r})$ and non-interacting kinetic energy $T_s[n]$, while the highest occupied eigenvalue equals minus the exact first ionization potential for the exact functional (Janak's and Almbladh-von Barth theorems).
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived by Euler-Lagrange minimization of the Hohenberg-Kohn energy functional partitioned as $F_{\mathrm{HK}}[n] = T_s[n] + E_H[n] + E_{xc}[n]$ with respect to orthonormal auxiliary orbitals $\psi_i^*(\mathbf{r})$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Formally exact in the ground state if the true $E_{xc}[n]$ is known. Kohn-Sham eigenvalues $\varepsilon_i$ are auxiliary Lagrange multipliers rather than true quasiparticle excitation energies, leading to the classic bandgap underestimation when semilocal approximations omit the derivative discontinuity.

V_{\\mathrm{eff}}(\\mathbf{r}).name: Kohn-Sham Effective Local Potential
V_{\\mathrm{eff}}(\\mathbf{r}).description: Self-consistent local potential combining external, Hartree, and exchange-correlation potentials.

\\psi_i(\\mathbf{r}).name: Kohn-Sham Auxiliary Orbital
\\psi_i(\\mathbf{r}).description: Normalized $i$-th single-particle eigenfunction whose squared modulus summed over occupied states yields the exact ground-state density.

\\varepsilon_i.name: Kohn-Sham Orbital Eigenvalue
\\varepsilon_i.description: Single-particle Lagrange multiplier eigenvalue of the $i$-th auxiliary Kohn-Sham state.

formulas.title: Kohn-Sham Effective and Exchange-Correlation Potential
formulas.equation: V_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{r}) = V_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathbf{r}) + V_H(\mathbf{r}) + V_{xc}(\mathbf{r}), \quad V_{xc}(\mathbf{r}) = \frac{\delta E_{xc}[n]}{\delta n(\mathbf{r})}
formulas.description: Decomposes the local Kohn-Sham effective potential $V_{\mathrm{eff}}(\mathbf{r})$ into the external nuclear potential $V_{\mathrm{ext}}(\mathbf{r})$, the classical Hartree electrostatic potential $V_H(\mathbf{r})$, and the exchange-correlation potential $V_{xc}(\mathbf{r})$ defined as the functional derivative of $E_{xc}[n]$ with respect to electron density $n(\mathbf{r})$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The effective field felt by each Kohn-Sham electron equals the external potential plus classical charge repulsion plus a quantum correction obtained by differentiating the exchange-correlation energy with respect to local density.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Every tricky quantum exchange and correlation effect is neatly bundled into a single local potential term obtained by asking how the exchange-correlation energy changes when you add a tiny sliver of charge at point r.
formulas.interpretation: Here $V_H(\mathbf{r}) = \frac{e^2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \int \frac{n(\mathbf{r}')}{|\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}'|} d^3r'$ is the classical Coulomb potential of the total density, so $V_{xc}(\mathbf{r})$ must simultaneously cancel Hartree self-interaction, encode Pauli exchange, capture dynamical Coulomb correlation, and absorb the kinetic difference $T[n] - T_s[n]$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises directly from taking the functional derivative $\delta E[n] / \delta n(\mathbf{r})$ of the partitioned Kohn-Sham total energy functional.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Far outside a finite neutral atom or molecule ($r \to \infty$), the exact $V_{xc}(\mathbf{r})$ decays asymptotically as $-e^2/(4\pi\varepsilon_0 r)$ to cancel self-interaction, whereas standard LDA and GGA potentials decay exponentially too fast, causing errors in Rydberg states and charge-transfer excitations.

V_{\\mathrm{eff}}(\\mathbf{r}).name: Kohn-Sham Effective Potential
V_{\\mathrm{eff}}(\\mathbf{r}).description: Total local multiplicative potential governing the auxiliary Kohn-Sham orbitals.

V_{\\mathrm{ext}}(\\mathbf{r}).name: External Potential
V_{\\mathrm{ext}}(\\mathbf{r}).description: Potential energy due to atomic nuclei and external electromagnetic fields.

V_H(\\mathbf{r}).name: Hartree Electrostatic Potential
V_H(\\mathbf{r}).description: Classical Coulomb repulsion potential generated by the electron density $n(\mathbf{r})$.

V_{xc}(\\mathbf{r}).name: Exchange-Correlation Potential
V_{xc}(\\mathbf{r}).description: Functional derivative of the exchange-correlation energy functional encoding all non-classical many-body interactions.

E_{xc}[n].name: Exchange-Correlation Energy Functional
E_{xc}[n].description: Universal functional capturing exchange, correlation, and the interacting-minus-noninteracting kinetic energy difference.

n(\\mathbf{r}).name: Electron Number Density
n(\\mathbf{r}).description: Spatial electron probability density normalized to the total electron count $N$.

formulas.title: Local Density Approximation (LDA) Exchange-Correlation Functional
formulas.description: Approximates the exact exchange-correlation energy functional $E_{xc}[n]$ by integrating the local electron density $n(\mathbf{r})$ multiplied by the exchange-correlation energy per electron $\varepsilon_{xc}^{\mathrm{unif}}(n)$ of a homogeneous electron gas evaluated at the local density.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The Local Density Approximation treats every tiny region of an inhomogeneous atom, molecule, or crystal as if it were a slice of a uniform electron gas having the same local density.
formulas.intuitive_summary: By borrowing the exact known quantum exchange and correlation energy of a uniform electron sea at each point in space, LDA turns DFT into a remarkably accurate workhorse for solids and molecules.
formulas.interpretation: Splitting $\varepsilon_{xc}^{\mathrm{unif}}(n) = \varepsilon_x^{\mathrm{unif}}(n) + \varepsilon_c^{\mathrm{unif}}(n)$ combines the exact Dirac exchange term $\varepsilon_x^{\mathrm{unif}}(n) = -\frac{3 e^2}{16\pi\varepsilon_0} (3n/\pi)^{1/3}$ with accurate quantum Monte Carlo parametrizations (Perdew-Zunger, Vosko-Wilk-Nusair) of Ceperley-Alder correlation data; its unexpected accuracy in inhomogeneous matter stems from satisfying the exact exchange-correlation hole sum rule.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Constitutes the first rung of Perdew's Jacob's ladder, derived from the slowly varying density expansion around the homogeneous jellium reference system.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Becomes asymptotically exact in the limit of slowly varying electron densities ($|\nabla n|/n^{4/3} \to 0$) and at high densities ($r_s \to 0$). Systematically overbinds molecules and solids (underestimating lattice constants by 1-2%), misses nonlocal van der Waals dispersion, and underestimates semiconductor bandgaps.

E_{xc}^{\\mathrm{LDA}}[n].name: LDA Exchange-Correlation Energy
E_{xc}^{\\mathrm{LDA}}[n].description: Approximate total exchange-correlation energy evaluated from the local uniform-gas energy density.

n(\\mathbf{r}).name: Local Electron Number Density
n(\\mathbf{r}).description: Three-dimensional electron density at spatial coordinate $\mathbf{r}$.

\\varepsilon_{xc}^{\\mathrm{unif}}(n).name: Uniform Electron Gas Exchange-Correlation Energy per Particle
\\varepsilon_{xc}^{\\mathrm{unif}}(n).description: Exact exchange plus QMC-calibrated correlation energy per electron of a homogeneous jellium gas of constant density $n$.

formulas.title: Identical-Particle Exchange Permutation Symmetry Postulate
formulas.description: Enforces the symmetrization postulate for an $N$-particle quantum wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf{x}_1,\dots,\mathbf{x}_N)$ under the pairwise particle-exchange operator $\hat{P}_{ij}$, requiring eigenvalue $+1$ for integer-spin bosons and $-1$ for half-integer-spin fermions.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Because identical quantum particles cannot be individually labeled, exchanging the space-spin coordinates of any pair $(i, j)$ must leave the physical ray unchanged, restricting states in three or more spatial dimensions to totally symmetric or totally antisymmetric representations of the symmetric group $S_N$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Swapping two identical particles never alters any measurable probability, so the wavefunction either stays identical (bosons) or flips its overall sign (fermions).
formulas.interpretation: Since $\hat{P}_{ij}^2 = \hat{I}$ and $[\hat{P}_{ij}, \hat{H}] = 0$ for any symmetric Hamiltonian, permutation parity is conserved under unitary time evolution. In relativistic quantum field theory, the spin-statistics theorem proves that the $+$ sign belongs exclusively to integer spin and the $-$ sign exclusively to half-integer spin.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Arises from invariance under the discrete permutation group $S_N$ of indistinguishable particles combined with the relativistic spin-statistics theorem.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Holds rigorously in $d \ge 3$ spatial dimensions where the fundamental group of configuration space is $S_N$. In strictly two-dimensional systems, the braid group replaces $S_N$ and permits arbitrary fractional exchange phases $e^{i\theta}$ (anyons).

\\hat{P}_{ij}.name: Pairwise Particle Exchange Operator
\\hat{P}_{ij}.description: Unitary, Hermitian transposition operator that swaps space-spin coordinates $\mathbf{x}_i \leftrightarrow \mathbf{x}_j$.

\\Psi(\\mathbf{x}_1,\\dots,\\mathbf{x}_N.name: Many-Body Wavefunction
\\Psi(\\mathbf{x}_1,\\dots,\\mathbf{x}_N.description: Joint probability amplitude for $N$ identical particles with space-spin coordinates $\mathbf{x}_k = (\mathbf{r}_k, \sigma_k)$.

\\mathbf{x}_k.name: Single-Particle Space-Spin Coordinate
\\mathbf{x}_k.description: Combined position vector $\mathbf{r}_k$ and discrete spin projection $\sigma_k$ of the $k$-th particle.

formulas.title: Slater Determinant Antisymmetric Fermion Wavefunction
formulas.description: Constructs the normalized, totally antisymmetric $N$-fermion wavefunction $\Psi(\mathbf{x}_1,\dots,\mathbf{x}_N)$ from $N$ orthonormal single-particle spin-orbitals $\phi_\alpha(\mathbf{x}_j)$ as a scaled $N \times N$ determinant.
formulas.conceptual_definition: A Slater determinant is the unique antisymmetrized product state of $N$ non-interacting fermions, automatically satisfying both normalization and the Pauli exclusion principle.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Arranging single-particle orbitals into a determinant guarantees that swapping any two fermions flips the sign of the state and trying to put two fermions into the same orbital collapses the amplitude to zero.
formulas.interpretation: Expanding the determinant sums over all $N!$ permutations $P \in S_N$ weighted by $\operatorname{sgn}(P)$, ensuring $\hat{P}_{ij}\Psi = -\Psi$. In Hartree-Fock theory, minimizing $\langle \Psi | \hat{H} | \Psi \rangle$ over single Slater determinants yields both direct Coulomb repulsion and the purely quantum Fock exchange interaction.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Generated by applying the antisymmetrization projector $\hat{\mathcal{A}} = (N!)^{-1} \sum_{P \in S_N} \operatorname{sgn}(P) \hat{P}$ to a Hartree product of orthonormal spin-orbitals.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Exact for all non-interacting fermion systems and serves as the reference vacuum for post-Hartree-Fock correlation methods; strongly correlated interacting states require linear combinations of multiple Slater determinants (configuration interaction).

\\Psi(\\mathbf{x}_1,\\dots,\\mathbf{x}_N.name: Antisymmetric N-Fermion Wavefunction
\\Psi(\\mathbf{x}_1,\\dots,\\mathbf{x}_N.description: Normalized totally antisymmetric probability amplitude for $N$ identical fermions.

\\phi_\\alpha(\\mathbf{x}_j).name: Single-Particle Spin-Orbital
\\phi_\\alpha(\\mathbf{x}_j).description: Normalized $\alpha$-th single-particle eigenfunction evaluated at the space-spin coordinate $\mathbf{x}_j$ of the $j$-th fermion.

N.name: Particle Number
N.description: Total number of identical fermions occupying $N$ distinct orthonormal spin-orbitals.

formulas.title: Fock Space Direct-Sum Hilbert Space Decomposition
formulas.description: Defines the many-body Fock space $\mathcal{F}$ as the orthogonal direct sum over all particle numbers $N \ge 0$ of the symmetric ($+$) bosonic or antisymmetric ($-$) fermionic $N$-particle Hilbert spaces $\mathcal{H}_N^{(\pm)}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Fock space provides a unified state space capable of describing quantum systems with variable or indefinite particle number, including coherent superpositions of states with different $N$.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Fock space stacks the zero-particle vacuum, one-particle states, two-particle states, and every higher-particle sector into one grand Hilbert space so operators can freely create and destroy particles.
formulas.interpretation: The $N=0$ sector $\mathcal{H}_0 \cong \mathbb{C}$ is spanned by the unique vacuum state $|0\rangle$, while $\mathcal{H}_N^{(\pm)} = \hat{S}_{\pm}\mathcal{H}_1^{\otimes N}$ is the properly symmetrized $N$-fold tensor power of the single-particle Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_1$. States with different $N$ are mutually orthogonal unless superposed as in coherent or BCS states.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Constructed from the symmetric or exterior tensor algebra over the single-particle Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_1$ to respect indistinguishability across all particle-number sectors.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Reduces to standard fixed-$N$ first-quantized quantum mechanics when restricted to a single sector $\mathcal{H}_N^{(\pm)}$ by a particle-number-conserving Hamiltonian $[\hat{H}, \hat{N}] = 0$; essential whenever particles are created, annihilated, or grand-canonically exchanged.

\\mathcal{F}.name: Many-Body Fock Space
\\mathcal{F}.description: Complete separable Hilbert space spanning all particle-number sectors for identical bosons or fermions.

\\mathcal{H}_N^{(\\pm)}.name: Symmetrized N-Particle Hilbert Space
\\mathcal{H}_N^{(\\pm)}.description: Symmetric ($+$) or antisymmetric ($-$) subspace of the $N$-fold tensor product of the single-particle Hilbert space.

N.name: Particle Number Sector Index
N.description: Non-negative integer labeling the eigenvalue of the total particle-number operator $\hat{N}$.

formulas.title: Canonical Multi-Mode Bosonic Commutation Algebra
formulas.description: Specifies the canonical commutation relations for multi-mode bosonic creation operators $\hat{a}_j^{\dagger}$ and annihilation operators $\hat{a}_i$ acting on the symmetric Fock space.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Multi-mode bosonic ladder operators generalize the harmonic-oscillator algebra so that independent modes commute while each mode obeys $[\hat{a}_i, \hat{a}_i^\dagger] = 1$, enforcing Bose-Einstein statistics and unrestricted mode occupancy.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Bosonic creation operators commute with one another, so the order in which you add identical bosons to states never introduces a minus sign and any number of bosons can pile into the same mode.
formulas.interpretation: Acting on an occupation-number eigenstate $|\dots, n_i, \dots\rangle$, these commutators imply $\hat{a}_i^{\dagger}|n_i\rangle = \sqrt{n_i + 1}|n_i + 1\rangle$ and $\hat{a}_i|n_i\rangle = \sqrt{n_i}|n_i - 1\rangle$, with number operator $\hat{n}_i = \hat{a}_i^{\dagger}\hat{a}_i$ having non-negative integer spectrum $n_i \in \{0, 1, 2, \dots\}$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Follows directly from canonical quantization of symmetric many-body modes and unitary preservation of the Heisenberg-Weyl algebra across independent single-particle orbitals.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Reduces to the single-mode quantum harmonic oscillator commutator $[\hat{a}, \hat{a}^{\dagger}] = 1$ when restricted to one mode. In the macroscopic occupation limit $n_i \gg 1$, the unit commutator becomes negligible relative to $\langle \hat{a}_i^{\dagger}\hat{a}_i \rangle$, recovering classical wave fields such as coherent laser light or the Gross-Pitaevskii condensate order parameter.

\\hat{a}_i.name: Bosonic Annihilation Operator
\\hat{a}_i.description: Dimensionless ladder operator that removes one boson from single-particle mode $i$.

\\hat{a}_j^{\\dagger}.name: Bosonic Creation Operator
\\hat{a}_j^{\\dagger}.description: Hermitian conjugate ladder operator that adds one boson to single-particle mode $j$.

\\delta_{ij}.name: Kronecker Delta
\\delta_{ij}.description: Discrete identity symbol equal to $1$ for $i = j$ and $0$ for $i \neq j$.

formulas.title: Canonical Fermionic Anticommutation Relations (Jordan-Wigner Algebra)
formulas.description: Defines the canonical anticommutation relations (CAR) for fermionic annihilation operators $\hat{c}_i$ and creation operators $\hat{c}_j^{\dagger}$, where $\{\hat{A}, \hat{B}\} = \hat{A}\hat{B} + \hat{B}\hat{A}$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: The fermionic anticommutation algebra encodes both total exchange antisymmetry and the Pauli exclusion principle directly inside the operator multiplication rules of antisymmetric Fock space.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Swapping two fermionic creation operators flips the sign of the state, and applying the same creation operator twice automatically gives zero, forbidding double occupancy.
formulas.interpretation: For $i = j$, $\{\hat{c}_i^{\dagger}, \hat{c}_i^{\dagger}\} = 0$ enforces $(\hat{c}_i^{\dagger})^2 = 0$, while $\hat{n}_i = \hat{c}_i^{\dagger}\hat{c}_i$ satisfies $\hat{n}_i^2 = \hat{n}_i$, restricting occupation eigenvalues strictly to $n_i \in \{0, 1\}$. For $i \neq j$, $\hat{c}_i^{\dagger}\hat{c}_j^{\dagger}|0\rangle = -\hat{c}_j^{\dagger}\hat{c}_i^{\dagger}|0\rangle$ reproduces Slater determinant antisymmetry.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Formulated by Jordan and Wigner as the unique Clifford-algebraic representation of antisymmetric exchange statistics in Fock space, preserved under all unitary single-particle basis transformations and canonical Bogoliubov transformations.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Holds identically for all nonrelativistic and relativistic spin-$1/2$ fermions (electrons, protons, neutrons, quarks) across arbitrary interaction strengths; mapped to spin-$1/2$ Pauli matrices in one dimension via the Jordan-Wigner string transformation.

\\hat{c}_i.name: Fermionic Annihilation Operator
\\hat{c}_i.description: Dimensionless operator that destroys one fermion in single-particle spin-orbital $i$.

\\hat{c}_j^{\\dagger}.name: Fermionic Creation Operator
\\hat{c}_j^{\\dagger}.description: Hermitian conjugate operator that creates one fermion in single-particle spin-orbital $j$.

\\delta_{ij}.name: Kronecker Delta
\\delta_{ij}.description: Discrete identity symbol equal to $1$ when $i = j$ and $0$ otherwise.

formulas.title: Second-Quantized Field Operator and Total Particle Number
formulas.description: Expands the local position-space field annihilation operator $\hat{\psi}(\mathbf{r})$ in any complete orthonormal single-particle basis $\phi_{\alpha}(\mathbf{r})$ and expresses the total particle-number operator $\hat{N}$ as the spatial integral of the number-density operator $\hat{\psi}^{\dagger}(\mathbf{r})\hat{\psi}(\mathbf{r})$.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Field operators transform discrete mode creation and annihilation operators into continuous spacetime-dependent operators that create or destroy localized particles at point $\mathbf{r}$, bridging first-quantized wave mechanics with quantum field theory.
formulas.intuitive_summary: Replacing expansion coefficients of a classical wavefunction with annihilation operators turns the wavefunction itself into a local quantum field whose squared modulus integrates to the total number of particles.
formulas.interpretation: Using completeness $\sum_\alpha \phi_\alpha(\mathbf{r})\phi_\alpha^*(\mathbf{r}') = \delta^{(3)}(\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}')$, the field operators obey equal-time canonical anticommutation (or commutation for bosons) relations $[\hat{\psi}(\mathbf{r}), \hat{\psi}^{\dagger}(\mathbf{r}')]_{\pm} = \delta^{(3)}(\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}')$, while orthonormality reduces $\hat{N} = \sum_\alpha \hat{c}_\alpha^{\dagger}\hat{c}_\alpha$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Derived via unitary basis transformation from an orthonormal single-particle Hilbert-space basis $\{\phi_\alpha\}$ to the continuous position eigenbasis $|\mathbf{r}\rangle$; invariant under global $U(1)$ phase rotations $\hat{\psi} \to e^{i\theta}\hat{\psi}$, which by Noether's theorem conserves $\hat{N}$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Valid in any spatial dimension with the appropriate volume element $d^d r$ and spin index $\sigma$. For a single-particle state $|\Psi\rangle = \int d^3r\,\Psi(\mathbf{r})\hat{\psi}^{\dagger}(\mathbf{r})|0\rangle$, $\langle 0 | \hat{\psi}(\mathbf{r}) | \Psi \rangle = \Psi(\mathbf{r})$ recovers the ordinary first-quantized wavefunction.

\\hat{\\psi}(\\mathbf{r}).name: Quantum Field Annihilation Operator
\\hat{\\psi}(\\mathbf{r}).description: Position-space operator that annihilates a particle at spatial coordinate $\mathbf{r}$.

\\phi_{\\alpha}(\\mathbf{r}).name: Orthonormal Single-Particle Basis Function
\\phi_{\\alpha}(\\mathbf{r}).description: Complete set of single-particle spatial wavefunctions indexed by quantum numbers $\alpha$.

\\hat{c}_{\\alpha}.name: Mode Annihilation Operator
\\hat{c}_{\\alpha}.description: Dimensionless annihilation operator for a particle in single-particle state $\alpha$.

\\hat{N}.name: Total Particle-Number Operator
\\hat{N}.description: Hermitian operator counting the total number of particles across all modes in Fock space.

formulas.title: Second-Quantized Interacting Many-Body Hamiltonian
formulas.description: Expresses an arbitrary interacting many-body Hamiltonian with one-body kinetic/external matrix elements $t_{ij}$ and two-body interaction matrix elements $V_{ijkl}$ in particle-number-independent second-quantized operator form.
formulas.conceptual_definition: Second quantization casts any symmetric sum of single-particle and pairwise interactions into a universal bilinear and quartic operator form whose matrix elements act identically across every particle-number sector of Fock space.
formulas.intuitive_summary: The first sum moves individual particles between orbitals with amplitude $t_{ij}$, while the second sum scatters pairs of particles from states $(k, l)$ into $(i, j)$ with interaction strength $V_{ijkl}$.
formulas.interpretation: Here $t_{ij} = \int d^3r\,\phi_i^*(\mathbf{r})\hat{h}_1(\mathbf{r})\phi_j(\mathbf{r})$ and $V_{ijkl} = \iint d^3r\,d^3r'\,\phi_i^*(\mathbf{r})\phi_j^*(\mathbf{r}')V(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}')\phi_k(\mathbf{r})\phi_l(\mathbf{r}')$. The reversed ordering $\hat{c}_l\hat{c}_k$ ensures normal-ordered sign consistency for fermions when deriving $\hat{V}$ from $\frac{1}{2}\iint \hat{\psi}^{\dagger}(\mathbf{r})\hat{\psi}^{\dagger}(\mathbf{r}')V(\mathbf{r}-\mathbf{r}')\hat{\psi}(\mathbf{r}')\hat{\psi}(\mathbf{r})\,d^3r\,d^3r'$.
formulas.symmetry_origin: Obtained by inserting the field-operator expansion into the normal-ordered first-quantized energy functional; automatically preserves permutation symmetry and global $U(1)$ particle-number conservation $[\hat{H}, \hat{N}] = 0$.
formulas.limits_and_boundary: Setting $V_{ijkl} = 0$ yields an exactly diagonalizable non-interacting gas; truncating to on-site lattice terms yields the Hubbard model, while restricting to opposite-momentum pair scattering yields the BCS pairing Hamiltonian.

\\hat{H}.name: Second-Quantized Many-Body Hamiltonian
\\hat{H}.description: Total energy operator acting on Fock space for an arbitrary number of interacting identical particles.

t_{ij}.name: One-Body Matrix Element
t_{ij}.description: Single-particle kinetic plus external-potential transition amplitude $\langle i | \hat{T} + \hat{U} | j \rangle$.

V_{ijkl}.name: Two-Body Interaction Matrix Element
V_{ijkl}.description: Pairwise interaction amplitude $\langle ij | \hat{V} | kl \rangle$ scattering particles from orbitals $(k, l)$ into $(i, j)$.

\\hat{c}_i^{\\dagger}.name: Orbital Creation Operator
\\hat{c}_i^{\\dagger}.description: Creation operator for single-particle orbital $i$ (fermionic $\hat{c}_i^{\dagger}$ or bosonic $\hat{a}_i^{\dagger}$).
